q: How do you tell one story to four different rooms?
lines: One company, one set of facts, one hard stretch behind it.
Four kinds of investor, each in the room for a different reason.
So four decks, and not one fact changes between them.
quote: Framing of the story mattered here as much as the facts
from: the work deck, on the early investors
close: We find what each room came for, and put that part of the truth first.
alt: The decks, laid out together

q: How do you ask for money when you are worth less than last time?
lines: A down round reads like a verdict.
So the price is not hidden, and not dressed up.
It is put beside everything that did not go down: the customers, the numbers, the people who keep coming back.
quote: Beloved underwear company in need of a refreshed story to raise a re-capitalization in a down round.
from: the work deck
close: We find what held its value, and build the ask on that.
alt: Key highlights: product leader, category pioneer, outstanding KPIs

q: How do you go back to the people who already believed in you?
lines: They were asked first, and they had the most to be sore about.
The story did not open with a pitch. It opened with why they came in at all.
And it named what broke without handing anyone the blame.
quote: market forces have driven tomboyx to the breaking point -- not past leadership or decisions that early investors may contextualize differently
from: a note on the early investors' deck
close: We start from what someone already feels, not from what we need them to do.
alt: The investment opportunity slide from the early investors' deck

q: How do you tell the truth about the bad years?
lines: Leave them out, and the first question in the room is about them.
Lead with them, and nothing after is heard.
So the past gets the room it needs and no more, and the rest goes to who is running it now.
quote: layout and minimal focus on the past draws attention to the team, versus individual players
from: a note on the syndicates' deck
close: We decide how much of the past a story has to carry.
alt: Run by a strong team

q: How do you change the story without changing the facts?
lines: The same numbers are in every deck.
What moves is which one comes first, what sits beside it, and what it is called.
Nothing is added. Nothing is bent.
quote: language captures the exceptional metrics while keeping warmth at the forefront
from: a note on the syndicates' deck
close: We keep the facts fixed and move everything else.
alt: Best in class premium basics KPIs

q: How do you make someone feel a company before they fund it?
lines: Some investors decide with a spreadsheet. Some decide when they recognise themselves.
For them the pictures come first, chosen with care about who is looking.
The numbers follow, as proof of a feeling they already have.
quote: Imagery nods to the female gaze in a deliberate repudiation of male gaze focused marketing.
from: the work deck, on the values-driven investors
close: We choose what is seen first for the person doing the seeing.
alt: The opportunity slide from the values-driven investors' deck

q: How do you make numbers mean something to someone outside your industry?
lines: A return rate means nothing if you have never sold underwear.
So every number sits next to the one it beats.
The investor does the sum themselves, and believes it more for that.
quote: highlighting strong metrics in a way accessible for investors unfamiliar with underwear sector
from: a note on the angels' deck
close: We put every number beside the thing that makes it readable.
alt: Transaction metrics, each with its comparison

q: How do you pitch when you are not in the room?
lines: A deck sent to a syndicate is passed on to people you will never meet.
Nobody is there to explain a slide.
So the colour, the size of a picture and the words on the page have to do the talking.
quote: Colors, language, size and style of imagery all contribute to the emotional resonance investors find with the deck.
from: the work deck, on the syndicates
close: We design for the reader the deck reaches after you have left.
alt: The work deck's page on the syndicates' deck

q: How do you let an investor know they are among their own?
lines: These investors came looking for a return and for their people.
A deck usually answers the first and leaves the second to chance.
This one answers both, in that order of feeling: who we are, then what it is worth.
quote: care about the market opportunity but also want to understand they are with "their" people
from: the work deck, on the values-driven investors
close: We say who a company is for, so the right people can tell it is them.
alt: The work deck's page on the values-driven investors' deck

q: How do you turn being loved into a reason to invest?
lines: Customers send this company invitations to their weddings.
That is usually a warm story for the last slide.
Here it is evidence, and it goes where the evidence goes.
quote: showcasing some of the recent wedding and graduation invites the company has received from fans
from: a note on the syndicates' deck
close: We treat affection as data, and show it like data.
alt: Honored to have an extended family: wedding and graduation invitations from customers

q: How do you get past the first no?
lines: Most pitches end at a screening, read by someone who will not make the decision.
That reader needs one thing they can carry upstairs.
So the deck is built around what is exceptional, and nothing ordinary is allowed to dilute it.
quote: a focus on the exceptional elements that make tomboyx special
from: the work deck, on the syndicates
close: We write for the person who has to repeat it to someone else.
alt: The value proposition slide

q: How do you sound like yourself in a document about money?
lines: An investor deck has a voice everyone expects.
This company has never sounded like that.
So the deck keeps the company's own strong words, and the design makes room for them.
quote: clear simple language and visuals appropriately support the intense words and strong brand ethos
from: a note on the early investors' deck
close: We keep a company's voice in the place it is most tempting to drop it.
alt: Brand equities: Original, Resolute, Intimate, Fearless, Ready

q: How do you take someone deep without losing them?
lines: Some investors want every number, and have run companies themselves.
A wall of metrics would be honest and unreadable.
So the data is walked through one question at a time, in the order they would ask.
quote: guiding investors through typical questions with a mix of data and narrative
from: a note on the angels' deck
close: We order the detail by the questions it answers.
alt: The work deck's page on the angels' deck

q: How do you show a market that has not happened yet?
lines: The case rests on a change in who buys, and why.
A claim like that is easy to wave away.
So it is counted: who is changing, how fast, and what they buy when they do.
quote: quantify market growth and the outcomes of LGBTQ consumer shifts
from: a note on the angels' deck
close: We turn a belief about the future into something you can check.
alt: A generational shift in identity

q: How do you remind someone why they cared?
lines: The first investors did not need convincing. They needed reminding.
The deck does not explain the company to them.
It says, without saying it: we are your people.
quote: reminder to investors of the values of the company implicitly saying, "we are your people"
from: a note on the early investors' deck
close: We work out what someone already knows, and do not tell them again.
alt: The brand manifesto slide

q: How do you prove you mean it?
lines: Any brand can say it is for every body.
This one sells XXS to XXXXXL.
So the claim is never left on its own. The size range is the sentence.
quote: reinforces the lived truth of the brand -- tomboyx supports XXS - XXXXXL with diverse silhouettes
from: a note on the early investors' deck
close: We find the fact that makes a value true, and show that.
alt: A TomboyX customer

q: How do you raise when the usual money was never coming?
lines: Very little venture money goes to founders like these.
That could be the excuse. The deck makes it the reason.
If the usual money is not coming, the people who do come are the story.
quote: language calls to the investors' values with a framing around the lack of traditional VC funding for women and queer founders
from: a note on the values-driven investors' deck
close: We turn what a company is missing into who it belongs to.
alt: The market, and the former leader losing it

q: How do you make a company in trouble look like the future?
lines: A company in a down round looks like yesterday.
The deck shows who is buying now, and how young they are.
The one shrinking is the old leader. This is the one the next generation picks.
quote: highlights the diversity of tomboyx--appeals to minority groups across generations
from: a note on the values-driven investors' deck
close: We show who a company is growing toward, not where it has been.
alt: A shifting market: why TomboyX is the brand of the future

q: How do you decide who to ask first?
lines: Four kinds of investor cannot all be asked at once.
The first ask went to the ones who already had feelings about the company.
What they did is what the next room got to see.
quote: the first audience solicited for new funds in the down round
from: the work deck, on the early investors
close: We plan the order of the rooms as carefully as the story in each.
alt: The work deck's page on the early investors' deck

q: How do you know a story is working?
lines: A story about a raise is only as good as the raise.
The test was plain: does it get past the screening, and in front of the person who decides.
It did.
quote: dramatically increased the emotional connection with the investors
from: the work deck, on the syndicates
close: We judge a story by what happens after it is told.
alt: Where the money raised would go
